subject: SpectraHealth — follow-up: ephemeral logs / retention exception request
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SpectraHealth discovery recap — ephemeral logs / retention follow-up

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations.

Key requirements you called out:
- No persistent storage of user prompts or model outputs (0-retention) unless explicitly allowed by patient consent or audit
- Minimal operational logs for debugging, but must be encrypted-at-rest, accessible only to SpectraHealth via KMS with restricted IAM
- Data residency: primary hosting in US-East, with EU-only option for PHI subsets in the future
- Audit evidence (audit logs, access logs) to support ePHI access requests and internal reviews

Proposed short-term path (pilot):
1) 0-retention for prompt+response payloads (default)
2) Short-lived ephemeral debug logs retained for 72 hours and then auto-purged — encrypted with customer KMS key
3) KV/cache diagnostics: store only hashed keys and metrics; full KV content retained for 24 hours in an encrypted buffer only for replaying failing sessions
4) Provide SOC2 and architecture diagram (attached) and a redline-friendly version of our retention exception template

Next steps I recommend:
- You: confirm whether 72h ephemeral window is acceptable for initial pilot or if you need 24h/48h
- Legal/Compliance at SpectraHealth: flag any non-starters for our proposed pilot language (I attached the DPH requirements doc you shared; we annotated in the attached spreadsheet)
- Redwood: Monica/Aditya will draft the exception language and a canary plan with rollback criteria

I’m blocking time for a 30 min follow-up on Tuesday 12/1 10:00–10:30 PT if that works — we can bring in security if you want.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(t): 415-555-0191
From: Elena Morris <elena@spectrahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@spectrahealth.com>, Legal Team <legal@spectrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SpectraHealth discovery recap — ephemeral logs / retention follow-up

Thanks, Tessa — good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) 0-retention on prompts/responses is our preference, but we need an operational escape hatch: if we discover a data-quality/regression issue that impacts safety, our SREs must be able to replay a specific session. Ideally the escape hatch is limited (token-level hashes + full payload for up to 24 hours) and gated by a legal/CSO approval flow.

2) 72h debug logs is on the long side for HI-PII classifications — can we offer 24h for PHI-labeled sessions and 72h for non-PHI? Our classification will be applied client-side before leaving the app to Redwood.

3) For audit evidence, SOC2 + syslog exports are required; can you confirm retention length of admin access logs and whether those are included in the same purge policy?

We’ll review the attachments and get Legal back with redlines. We are generally open to a pilot with strict controls, but our security team will want the KMS separation and an attestation that Redwood staff cannot access decrypted debug payloads.

Elena
Director of Product Security
SpectraHealth
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: SpectraHealth discovery recap — ephemeral logs / retention follow-up

Folks — forwarding Elena’s notes. Quick internal take:

- We can support a 24h max for PHI sessions and 72h for non-PHI by applying a retention-class tag at ingestion; leverage prefix/KV caching that already supports TTLs per-tag. Implementation effort: small config + gating in the control plane.
- KMS: we need customer-provided key (BYOK) for the debug buffer; otherwise we can rotate keys and provide strong access controls, but not full separation. SpectraHealth explicitly asked that Redwood staff cannot decrypt — only possible with BYOK and strict key policy (we should flag HSM support).
- Admin/syslog exports: those are retained 365d by default for internal observability; we can carve out a shorter retention window for SpectraHealth for admin logs tied to model inference (proposed: 90d) but audit logs for access must be retained per compliance needs — we should offer a view export and time-bounded retention for non-admin logs.

Proposed negotiation position to present to Elena:
1) Pilot: 24h PHI buffer (BYOK required), 72h non-PHI debug buffer (BYOK optional), auto-purge; locked down IAM; replay gated by SpectraHealth-approved runbook and legal ticket.
2) Admin logs: offer a 90d retention carveout; full access logs (who accessed the KMS/decryption) retained 1 year for compliance and available on export.
3) Canary policy: after 4 weeks without incidents we consider 24h/72h policy standard for SpectraHealth; incident criteria for rollback must be defined and documented.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll draft exception language + technical implementation notes for Tessa to share.

— Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SpectraHealth discovery recap — ephemeral logs / retention follow-up

Adding a quick implementation checklist for the exception draft:
- Add per-session metadata tag (phi_level: PHI | PII | NON_PHI) as part of ingest API.
- Enforce TTL in control plane: PHI -> 24h, NON_PHI -> 72h. Configurable per-contract.
- BYOK flow: integrate HSM-backed key import + customer KMS ARN; ensure we store only wrapped keys.
- Replay gating: require signed approval ticket from SpectraHealth (sso + legal approval) and log replay event in immutable audit log.
- Admin export behavior: build export endpoint and S3 signed-url delivery for one-off compliance requests.

I’ll spin up a short tech note (1 pager) and attach to the exception language. Also agree we should firm up rollback criteria and incident SLAs (e.g., detection window, notification targets).

— Aditya
Staff Engineer, Security & Platform Integrations
From: Elena Morris <elena@spectrahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@spectrahealth.com>, Legal Team <legal@spectrahealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SpectraHealth discovery recap — ephemeral logs / retention follow-up

Thanks everyone — that approach is promising and addresses many of our concerns. A few asks before we kick off a pilot: 

- SpectraHealth will require BYOK for PHI buffers and a documented replay approval flow (we will supply the ticketing system integration).
- Please provide the SOC2 report and the architecture diagram with the KMS flow redlined (we need to share with our InfoSec review board) — the HubSpot link you sent is fine but we need a downloadable artifact.
- Legal: we’ll send redlines on the exception template; please highlight any clauses that are non-negotiable on Redwood’s side.

Assuming the above, we’re happy to run a 6-week pilot starting week of 12/6. Tessa — please schedule security and engineering sync once we have the draft exception language.

Elena
